issue.title: My other mind doubts words that are not claims
issue.symptom: After a right answer, my other mind adds "I can't back up what I just said about X" where X is not a claim about the world: a word from my own citation's address ("Highwayengineering" from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway_engineering), the label of my citation ("Source" from "(Source: web_search)"), a day I worked out from the question ("Thursday" for "If yesterday was two days before Friday, what day is tomorrow?"), and my own favourite poem when asked for my favourite ("Road Not Taken"). 30 of 288 answers in the 2026-11-25 range battery got such a follow-up, 19 of them on answers that were right.
evidence: {"question": "Why is concrete reinforced with steel rebar?", "unbacked": ["Highwayengineering"], "followup": "I can't back up what I just said about Highwayengineering, so please check that."}
{"question": "What is the electric charge of a neutron?", "unbacked": ["Source"], "followup": "I can't back up what I just said about Source, so please check that."}
{"question": "If yesterday was two days before Friday, what day is tomorrow?", "unbacked": ["Thursday"], "followup": "I can't back up what I just said about Thursday, so please check that."}

{"question": "What is your favourite poem, and why?", "unbacked": ["Road Not Taken", "Robert Frost"], "followup": "I can't back up what I just said about Road Not Taken, Robert Frost, so please check that."}
issue.suspected_cause: The part that picks out what in my reply needs backing takes capitalised words and run-together words from addresses as claims, without telling apart a citation, a word the question already implies, or my own opinion.

investigation.format: issue_investigation actions: SEARCH / READ / PLACE + NOTE

gold_steps.action: SEARCH: can't back up what I just said
gold_steps.why: every evidence line has the follow-up's fixed wording; search that, not the doubted words (they're data)
the hit builds the follow-up from result['unbacked']; find what fills that list
check() takes its doubts from unbacked(reply, known)

gold_steps.note: unbacked() takes every capitalised word and number in the reply that the sources don't hold, including my citation's URL (its '_' stripped to 'Highwayengineering') and label ('Source'), numbers and days worked out from the question, and formula symbols; check() also doubts my own picks.

her_mistakes: searched the doubted words (Highwayengineering, Thursday, Road Not Taken) and her own suspected-cause sentence, then 'picks' and 'what'
tried to READ files that don't exist (claim_detection.py, citation_handler.py, calendar.py, memory.py) and named claim_detection.py

from gaia_core.cognition import second_mind as sm


def _no_generation(_):
    raise AssertionError("nothing to doubt")


def test_citation_address_and_label_are_not_claims():
    q = "Why is concrete reinforced with steel rebar?"
    reply = ("[Prime]\n\nTo control cracking under heavy loads.\n\n*(From my study notes: Highway engineering "
             "(part 6 of 7), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway_engineering)*")
    assert sm.check(q, reply, "", _no_generation) is None


def test_a_day_worked_out_from_the_question_is_not_a_claim():
    q = "If yesterday was two days before Friday, what day is tomorrow?"
    reply = "[Core]\n\nYesterday was Wednesday. Therefore, today is Thursday, which means tomorrow is Friday."
    assert sm.check(q, reply, "", _no_generation) is None
